issues.description: Silent semantic change: coerceNumber maps null/undefined/NaN to 0 where original code propagated null/NaN through arithmetic.
issues.detail: The original panLinear/zoomLinear used identity + toNumber, so non-numeric domain entries flowed through as null/NaN. The new coerceNumber substitutes 0 via `?? 0`, changing observable output for malformed inputs. This is a postcondition shift smuggled into a 'just types' PR. State the policy explicitly or preserve NaN propagation.

issues.description: panLog/zoomLog read domain[0] before the non-emptiness guard, defeating the invariant.
issues.detail: Math.sign(domain[0]) executes outside the inner pan/zoom call, so an empty domain produces Math.sign(undefined) = NaN before isNonEmpty ever fires. The precondition is asserted in the wrong place. Hoist the non-empty check to the public boundary so the invariant holds once, uniformly across all entry points.

issues.description: Parameter type number[] overstates what the implementation actually constrains given lift/ground polymorphism.
issues.detail: The original code was polymorphic in lifted values; date-like or string-numeric domains flowed through. Narrowing to number[] / [number, number] asserts a value model never enforced at runtime, while the real invariant (length >= 2) is under-specified. Either validate at the edge with NonEmptyArray on the signature, or keep the type honest.

issues.description: Empty-domain throw is a new policy decision bundled into a typing refactor.
issues.detail: The PR claims same runtime behavior but introduces a throw for empty domains where callers previously got NaN propagation. Policy changes deserve their own change with a note for downstream consumers. Separate the value-precondition decision from the type annotation pass.

issues.description: Tests cover only panLinear/zoomLinear empty-domain error; six other entry points are unproved.
issues.detail: panLog, panPow, panSymlog, zoomLog, zoomPow, zoomSymlog share the same precondition but no test exercises it. Two tests do not establish the invariant for eight functions, particularly given the panLog/zoomLog guard-ordering bug above. Add coverage for every entry point that now throws.

issues.description: peek overload promises non-undefined T but the implementation cannot discharge that proof.
issues.detail: The overload peek<T>(readonly [T, ...T[]]): T only fires when callers already proved non-emptiness in types, which internal pan/zoom call sites do not. Under noUncheckedIndexedAccess the implementation would not type-check. A comment on intended use, or a runtime assertion, would close the gap.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on a clean verdict: this is a faithful type-annotation pass with two quiet behavioral changes that escape the 'just types' framing. coerceNumber silently maps null/undefined/NaN to 0 where the original propagated null, and a new empty-domain throw replaces NaN propagation — both are policy decisions, not typing. The empty-domain guard is also misplaced for panLog/zoomLog, which read domain[0] before the check fires, and the number[] signature overstates what the implementation actually constrains. Test coverage for the new error path exercises only two of eight entry points. Fix the guard placement, document or revert the coercion choice, and expand tests before merge.
